what_it_is: Modelled output of oil-fired back-up generators in Nigeria. About 9 GW of back-up capacity. Sub-Saharan Africa as a whole is given as 40 TWh from 40 GW, equal to 8% of electricity generation.
do_not: Do not add this 2018 model result to a 2024 grid total.

source: World Bank, Diesel Power Generation study (2014), citing the Nigeria low-carbon study
what_it_is: 16,360 GWh of self-generation in 2009, covering diesel, gas and gasoline generators.
do_not: This is a cited earlier study, not a new measurement in the 2014 inventory.

source: World Bank, Diesel Power Generation study (2014)
what_it_is: Authors' own cross-sector range, 5,240 to 20,380 GWh. Sectors are for different years. The width is mostly the commercial-sector method. They warn that aggregating across sectors is not accurate and was done only for scale.
do_not: Do not replace the range with its midpoint.

source: World Bank, Diesel Power Generation study (2014)
what_it_is: Diesel gensets only, 3,262 to 3,423 GWh, across telecoms, manufacturing, oil and gas, residential and commercial. Gasoline generators are largely outside this total.
do_not: This is not total captive generation. Gasoline sets are a large part of household use.

source: IFC, The Dirty Footprint of the Broken Grid (2019), summary
what_it_is: Conservative estimate of installed back-up generator capacity in Nigeria, 15-20 GW, against grid capacity of 5-15 GW in the same sentence.
do_not: Capacity, not annual energy. Do not convert to TWh without a capacity factor the study states.

source: IFC, The Dirty Footprint of the Broken Grid (2019), full report
what_it_is: Survey-adjusted fleet: 2.8 million residential and 210 thousand commercial sites, 13 GW, described as twice the installed capacity of power plants on the grid, and $5.4 billion a year of fuel spend. Nigeria is also given as 16% of back-up energy service among the low- and middle-income countries in the model. The report does not print a Nigeria TWh next to that share, so none is derived here.
do_not: Do not multiply the 16% share by the regional TWh and present the product as IFC's Nigeria total.
